newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures spent another lacklustre session tracking Bunds within a narrow range and traders predicted a similar day's trading on Thursday.

The March bond future survived an early test of support below 131 and meandered along until a spurt late in the session, driven mainly by intra-day traders aiming to fill a "gap" left on charts at the open.
Once successfully filled, the contract drifted lower, again in tandem with the Bund futures, to settle at 131.06, down 0.14 on the day and little changed from the opening level of 131.02.
"There's nothing new in this market, volume's low and people are moving it around because they can," a trader at a large French bank said.
"Nothing happened, its a range market, we just had speculators playing the (chart) points and there's nothing more to wait for before Friday," the head of a brokerage said.
Traders said U.S. producer price data due for release on Friday remained the main focus for the French bond market given the current speculation about the possibility of a U.S. rate hike on March 25.
Traders said in the absence of any major events much of the action on Wednesday was rolling into the June bond contract ahead from the March contract ahead of its expiry on March 17.

There was little reaction to comments coming from the Franco-German summit in Lyon on Wednesday. Economists and traders said the reaffirmation of commitment to starting European monetary union on time was expected.

"Nothing stands out. The market expected them to get together and slap each others backs and stress their commitment to Maastricht," David Brickman, economist at Yamaichi International said. "They're not exactly going to say anything different."

Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said the talks had not addressed the question of delaying the start of European monetary union and finance ministers of both countries stressed their commitment to meeting the entry criteria on time.
Analysts and traders said officials were no doubt under strict orders to play down any hint of delay and rumours would, nevertheless, continue to circulate for some months to come.

"I think all central bankers have been told not to stir the shark pool," Nick Stephens at Credit Lyonnais Rouse said. "We're going to get two to three months of (delay speculation), although the effect of these rumours will dilute overtime."
The 10-year spread between French and German yields was little changed at minus 11 basis points as the benchmark 5.5 percent 2007 OAT yield climbed four basis points to 5.56 percent.

In addition to the Treasury's auction of 300 to 500 million Ecu of 2007 OATs on Thursday, market sources also said there was a possibility a planned 10-year franc Eurobond issue from Portugal could come tomorrow. The issue will be lead managed by CDC Marche, BNP and Lehman Brothers.
The franc slipped slightly against the mark to 3.3738 compared with 3.3712 late on Tuesday. It gained ground against the dollar reaching 5.7360, up from 5.7435.
Economists said no change in interest rates was expected after the Bank of France's regular monetary policy council meeting on Thursday.
